@BrianneKohl @amandadeibert Been there done that but at a law firm & I was a baby lawyer. But my peace of mind was more important. #MeToo movement has proved me right, have gained so many allies since then, powerful amazing people. Would not go back on my decision for anything.

@aharbo @JHWeissmann Earth Day was way less observed in the 80s, came back in 90s, ERA failed (my state #Virginia just ratified it), women still faced #MeToo stuff though we didn't call it that in 1970s-1990s, racism became more subtle, & the inequality gap started escalating in 1980s. Record is meh.

@quinncy Oh well long story short I bailed on 'curing the common cold' to do IPO law, got #MeToo'ed out of that, farted around in my late 20s - early 30s then did parent care from 34-46 (only child, single, never married no kids). I've had a good life but my career was hardly noteworthy.

...heck look at all the women (& men) who didn't come forward with their #MeToo experiences until later, their 40s, 50s, 60s & beyond (including myself). I'm just glad to see younger women & younger men questioning & shutting this all down sooner & sparing everyone a lot of pain.

@kellyyanghk My legal #MeToo incident was harassment in my 1st job as a patent attorney in a boutique IP law firm in Houston in 1997. I definitely believe you, I know what it is to abandon a career, but I am glad you have spoken up & I hope you find great strength & solidarity here on Twitter
@MiraSorvino please give this a read. And thanks again for speaking up when you did, because #MeToo is giving younger women the courage to have a #MySchoolToo movement.
1000% true & it's when this discomfort reaches a social critical mass we get empowering movements & changes the latest of which are #MeToo & #MySchoolToo
